title: UCB CS70: Discrete Math and Probability Theory

unit.title: Stable Matching as an Executable Contract
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student developing production-oriented software-engineering skill
unit.scope: A bounded kickoff connecting logic and proof to a robust implementation of left-proposing deferred acceptance.
learning_objectives: Turn a mathematical definition into explicit input contracts, output guarantees, and implementation invariants.
Implement deterministic left-proposing deferred acceptance for complete strict preferences.
Justify termination, stability, proposer optimality, and asymptotic cost under stated assumptions.
Build an independent stability oracle and deterministic tests that can expose implementation errors.
Document failure behavior, reproducibility, and the boundary between the mathematical model and a reusable software component.
required_learner_evidence: A runnable implementation with a documented public interface
Automated deterministic tests, including malformed-input and property-oriented cases
A design note containing contracts, invariants, proof arguments, and complexity analysis
Written responses to the supplied comprehension prompts
excluded_scope: Completion of CS70 or of any substantial fraction of the cataloged 60-hour course
Claims that this task reproduces an official UC Berkeley lecture, note, textbook chapter, or assignment
Matching with ties, incomplete preference lists, capacities, strategic behavior, or distributed deployment
Graph theory, number theory, polynomial rings, coding theory, probability, hashing, and load balancing

critical_conditions: The implementation is runnable using the submitted instructions.
For valid inputs, the output is a bijection and has no blocking pair.
The learner's proof and test evidence are their own and contain no hidden examiner material.
unit_completion_requires.validator_authority: Only a validator controlled by the worker harness may record completion.

completion_policy.on_unit_pass: Record completion only for kickoff_01_stable_matching_engineering; keep the course status partial.
completion_policy.on_unit_fail: Preserve the attempt and examiner evidence; do not infer completion from prose or file presence.
completion_policy.course_completion_rule: This kickoff can never, by itself, complete the course. Later independently validated units and an explicit course-level completion decision are required.

provenance.derivation_note: The topic choice uses the catalog's stated logic-proof/stable-matching correspondence. The activity design, requirements, explanations, and assessment are newly authored and are not represented as official UC Berkeley material.
